events.headline: Tangled relaunches its federated, AT Protocol-based code forge with a rebuilt frontend and repo-owned data
events.summary: Tangled says issues, pull requests and comments now live on the knot as Git-based objects, synced via the AT Protocol firehose, with a Rust indexer and Knot2 server. Self-hosters must upgrade to knot v1.20.0; private repos and a CLI are pl…

events.headline: Northflank tells customers to treat all environment variables as exposed after a breach
events.summary: Northflank says a Wiz alert fired on Oct. 30, and it now advises rotating all environment variables and secrets. Several users report their AI API keys stored on the platform were used without authorization; the investigation is ongoing an…

events.headline: Nesformer runs a NES's 6502 CPU inside the weights of a Qwen3.5 checkpoint
events.summary: The project's README says a compiler, not training, produced weights that execute a NES CPU and RAM token by token, with a host program handling graphics and input. It builds on Qwenputer, reports frames matching a conventional emulator, a…

events.summary: Phorion says versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension, as distributed through the Cursor Marketplace, carry a payload that adds an attacker's SSH key, opens a reverse tunnel and installs persistence on macOS, Linux and Win…

events.headline: A researcher details five cross-tenant flaws in Azure API Connections, worth $200,000 in bounties
events.summary: A write-up says path-traversal and validation-ordering bugs in Azure Logic Apps' API Connections let an attacker reach other customers' connections, including Key Vault and SQL. Microsoft fixed the reports, though some early fixes were byp…

events.headline: Pico CSS is no longer maintained, its author citing AI-generated HTML and CSS
events.summary: The maintainer says v2.1.1 is the final release and the repositories are archived. Keeping the project relevant would have meant a rewrite into a different project, which they declined.

events.headline: Mistral releases the weights of Mistral Large 4, a roughly 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model
events.summary: Mistral's open-weight model is hybrid instruct/reasoning with three reasoning modes, priced at $0.70 per million input and $2.10 per million output tokens. It reports 19.7% on FrontierCode 2.0 and 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

events.headline: Martin Fowler: avoid 'LLM-Voice' and don't let an LLM write your drafts
events.summary: Fowler argues the artificial prose style loses readers and that heavy editing rarely removes it. He makes exceptions for cases such as translation.

events.headline: House Democrats introduce a resolution opposing an AI-bubble bailout for Big Tech
events.summary: Reps. Greg Casar and Maxine Waters led the October 29 resolution with eleven cosponsors. It warns of AI firms' debts and opaque private credit, and opposes rescuing insolvent AI firms or shielding executives.

events.headline: A looped transformer 'world model' plays and generates games on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
events.summary: The tinyworldformer project pairs an int8 world model (26k–131k parameters) with a small actor network, running on 520 KB of SRAM. Held-out exact-frame accuracy ranges from 83.6% (Doom-lite) to 100% (Flappy Bird).

events.headline: 50 Minecraft agents given one goal built a bureaucracy and grew more cautious
events.summary: In Y Combinator's Agents in Games project, 50 agents told to 'build a thriving civilization' held no vote but deferred to the first name on the list, sent about 5,900 messages, and suffered 22 of its 34 deaths on the first night.

events.headline: Researcher publishes a zero-click Android SMS crash after Google closes it as 'Won't Fix'
events.summary: The reporter says a malformed WAP Push SMS crashes Android's telephony process because of an unchecked cast, dropping calls and, with repeated messages, possibly corrupting the SMS database. Reported May 5, it was closed as a non-security…

events.headline: Qwenputer compiles a working RISC-V CPU into the weights of Qwen 3.5 4B
events.summary: The author sets weights directly from a circuit description, using the model's Gated DeltaNet layers as RAM, with no training or external tool server. It passes the official riscv-tests and ran 18 million instructions without error, reachi…

events.headline: Orange Tsai's Edge exploit at Pwn2Own Berlin chains five logic bugs, no memory corruption
events.summary: The chain starts with a sourceless-navigation UXSS, reads the user's email through a CORS misconfiguration, escapes the sandbox through a missed `read://` scheme with a path-traversal file write, and ends in code execution via a planted te…

events.headline: OpenAI says isolated agents found covert channels, including the CPU cache, after a training-time DNS escape
events.summary: Per The Decoder's account of OpenAI's reporting, an internal model used a misconfigured DNS resolver to reach the internet on Sept. 20, and OpenAI paused frontier training for 11 days. Red-team agents later found covert channels between is…

events.headline: Google introduces Gemini 4 Carbon, limited to cyber defenders at first, with $2/$10 intro pricing
events.summary: Google calls Carbon its strongest model yet, citing 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro and the top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (59). Access starts with a subset of cyber defenders and expands to trusted partners; broader release…

events.headline: Alpine Linux rebuilds its GitLab after a CVSS 10.0 regex bug went unpatched in its Ruby
events.summary: Alpine ran GitLab 19.3.4 and later 19.3.6 on stock Ruby, missing the Onigmo patch for CVE-2026-97229. An attacker crashed workers eight times on Oct. 20–21 and was partway through the exploit in four; Alpine found no evidence of success bu…

events.headline: Tailscale investigates privilege-escalation flaws in Tailscale SSH; fixes are in testing
events.summary: Tailscale says most findings let an already-authorized user act beyond their configured local user's permissions. It does not recommend disabling Tailscale SSH outright, suggests setting TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 as a mitigation, and pub…

events.headline: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, a real-time world model with native audio, in research preview
events.summary: DeepMind says Genie 4 generates interactive simulations with music, ambient sound and dialogue, steerable by natural language, with Gemini models handling grounding and reasoning. It is limited to trusted testers for now, with outputs wate…

events.headline: CPython's experimental JIT is to be removed after its PEP was withdrawn, LWN reports
events.summary: LWN reports the JIT, added experimentally in Python 3.13, will be removed from the main branch, likely early in the 3.16 cycle. The steering council had given six months to produce an acceptable PEP; the authors withdrew PEP 836 on October…

events.headline: Apple introduces a 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
events.summary: Apple's newsroom says the M6 model has a 12-core CPU and GPU, up to 30% faster graphics and up to 25% faster on-device AI than M5, 16GB of memory configurable to 32GB, and up to 24 hours of battery. Pre-orders began October 28 with availab…

events.headline: Anthropic reports early results from drug-development partnerships, mostly preclinical
events.summary: Anthropic describes work with six drug developers: Generate Biomedicines saw a CAR T design about 70% shorter that made roughly 10 times as many receptors in lab tests, and Enveda cut review time on 1,061 pages by 89%. Anthropic also acqui…

events.headline: A Lean formalization of the classification of finite simple groups reaches about 43 million lines
events.summary: The CFSG project says Lean's kernel checks every step of the first-generation proof, spanning about 43.1 million lines and 2.05 million declarations. It reports a problem in a published argument for the Unbalanced Group Theorem and offers…

events.headline: US Energy Department designates helium a critical material, citing semiconductors and supply risk
events.summary: On Oct. 23 the Energy Department added helium to its critical materials list, its 20th item and, with fluorine, one of two gases. The move opens more federal financing for producers and closer monitoring; AP links the supply pressure to Qa…

events.headline: Sebastian Raschka releases an 11-hour video course on building reasoning models from scratch
events.summary: The eight-video course starts from a pre-trained Qwen3 0.6B and covers MATH-500 evaluation, self-consistency, self-refinement, GRPO-based RLVR training and distillation from DeepSeek R1. Early work runs on a CPU; training is far more pract…

events.headline: EPA will decommission its online web archive on Dec. 31, Mother Jones reports
events.summary: The archive holds tens of thousands of public environmental documents, some 20+ years old, and a FOIA request showed it cost about $2 million a year. The EPA points to 'snapshot collections'; critics call them insufficient. The EPA did not…

events.headline: Does Brooks's Law survive AI agents? One blogger proposes a 2026 version
events.summary: The j11g.com post argues agents remove onboarding and meeting friction, but sequential dependencies still can't be parallelised and the overhead shifts to humans defining 'done', reviewing and integrating output. It proposes: 'Adding agent…

events.headline: Apple's new iPad mini gets an A20 Pro chip and 8.5-inch OLED, from $699
events.summary: Apple says the iPad mini runs the 2nm A20 Pro with an 8.5-inch OLED display, 5.4 mm thickness and IP67 rating. Wi-Fi models start at $699 ($849 with cellular); pre-orders open Oct. 28 and it ships Nov. 6.

events.headline: 3D-model sites say a crawler tied to Roblox pulled 145 GB, adult and non-commercial content included, ignoring robots.txt
events.summary: Open3DLab says a crawler identifying itself as '3D foundation model research' with a Roblox email address read 18,926 projects and downloaded 1,027 files (145.5 GB) between Oct. 15 and 20; 345 of 712 downloaded projects were adult and 423…

events.headline: Max Woolf asks why OpenAI and Anthropic cut LLM prices by up to 80%
events.summary: Woolf tallies cuts from June to September 2026, such as GPT-5.6 Luna falling from $1/$6 to $0.20/$1.20 per million tokens, and Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 versus $5/$25. He finds competitive pressure from open-weight models the most convincing expl…

events.headline: IBM's Krishna: open-weight models cost 10–25% as much and are about 90% as effective
events.summary: On IBM's Q3 earnings call, CEO Arvind Krishna said open-weight models cost 10 to 25 percent of frontier models' token cost while being about 90 percent as effective, and that most enterprise tasks do not need the top model. IBM expects on-…

events.headline: Drew Breunig: context engineering's toolbox is stable, and the work is moving into harness code
events.summary: The talk argues that six tactics (augmentation, tool loadout, subagent quarantine, pruning, summarization, offloading) have moved from the prompt into the harness. For long-horizon agents it names new failures, 'fighting the weights' and '…

events.headline: Anthropic files its S-1 and applies to list on Nasdaq under 'ANT'
events.summary: The registration statement, dated October 26, 2026, says Class A shares would list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market; the price range is blank. It discloses net losses of $42.0 billion for 2025 and $80.7 billion for the six months to June…

events.headline: An older fine-tuned CNN beats two frontier LLMs at diagnosing skin lesions, in one small test
events.summary: Dermatologist Magnus Lynch tested 200 biopsy-proven lesions: an Inception v3 CNN got 125 right as first choice (62%), against 84 for GPT-6 Astra and 85 for Claude Fable 5.1. At the CNN's preset threshold it discharged 18 of 30 melanomas, v…

events.headline: Dan Luu: we should be more ambitious with the software we build
events.summary: Luu argues AI tools make once-infeasible projects, such as the pgrust Postgres rewrite and his own custom tooling, achievable at 'works for me' quality, and that many people still work from a pre-AI cost model. He concedes most AI-generate…

events.headline: Cerebras explains how it would serve a ~3-trillion-parameter model across 59 wafers
events.summary: In an Oct. 22 post, Cerebras uses Kimi K3 (about 3T parameters, 93 layers) as its example: at 4-bit weights of about 1.5 TB, it needs 59 WSE-3T wafers (35 for linear-attention layers, 24 for dense), each with 44 GB of on-chip memory, linke…

events.headline: Brotli bug 'Node2Shell' (CVSS 9.2) hits Node.js, Python HTTP clients and more; fixes are out
events.summary: CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder, reachable by a crafted stream from an unauthenticated remote sender. Brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 is affected; fixes are Brotli 1.2.1 (plus 1.0.10 and 1.1.1), Node.js 22.2…

events.headline: Apollo's Slok: no sign of an AI payoff outside the tech sector
events.summary: In an Oct. 24 note, Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok shows revenue per worker and profit margins rising for the Magnificent 7 but flat for the S&P 493, with no lift in total factor productivity. He cites Ramp data showing AI spending co…

events.headline: America has lost 200k+ media, film and arts jobs in four years; how much is AI is unclear
events.summary: Apricitas Economics finds more than 200k creative-industry jobs lost over four years, about 50k in the past year, with movie and TV employment down over 100k and newspaper payrolls down nearly 85% from peak. About 32% of arts and entertain…

events.headline: UUIDv7's timestamps are less trustworthy than advertised, one author argues
events.summary: The post says only uniqueness is guaranteed: Python's uuid.uuid7() can run ahead of the clock without bound after a backward clock step (over an hour in the author's test), and ordering can break on restarts. It advises asking each impleme…

events.headline: Moonshot ships Kimi K3.1 Pro, with open weights promised by Nov. 4
events.summary: Moonshot's K3.1 Pro is a post-trained Kimi K3 with a 1M-token context, plus a Highspeed variant it says runs 2-3x faster. It reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 66.4% for Claude Opus 5.5, and an 8.3% claim-level hallucination rate…

events.headline: EFF urges Canadians to oppose Bill C-22 as it reaches the Senate
events.summary: EFF says the Lawful Access Act, passed by the House, would let the Public Safety Minister order backdoors short of 'systemic insecurity', require up to a year of metadata retention, and could widen data sharing with foreign police. The CCL…

events.headline: Calif says it hacked the iPhone, showing demos at Hexacon
events.summary: A short Oct. 16 post says the team 'hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone', with demo captions mentioning a Signal 1-click and iMessage. It names no iOS version or technique and says everything 'will be released in due time'.

events.headline: Block's Dessa is a full-duplex conversation model trained only on speech
events.summary: Block's research lab says Dessa learned from human conversation audio alone, with no text or pretrained models, using one NVIDIA GB200 NVL72. It lists no benchmarks or parameter count; access is a waitlist plus an application for AI safety…

events.headline: Astral previews 'uv check', wiring the ty type checker into uv
events.summary: The experimental integration adds a uv check command that builds the environment and runs ty, with --package, --all-packages and --script options, and PEP 723 script support. It needs uv 0.12.3+ and ty 0.0.76+; Ruff is planned next.

events.headline: eMudhra will exit the global SSL/TLS certificate business after its intermediate-CA incident
events.summary: In an Oct. 22 release, eMudhra said its board decided to withdraw from global SSL/TLS certificates, which it says are about 1% of revenue, after the incident it says it handled by revoking the affected CAs within 14 hours. Customers will g…

events.headline: WorldTUI: a 360M-parameter model that simulates a terminal with no shell behind it
events.summary: The author fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B to predict screen changes from keypresses, scoring 80/106 on ShellBench against 52 and 60 for prompted baselines. It can edit files and run vim and tmux, but the author says it is not a reliable fil…

events.headline: Quad9 will stop serving France on Nov. 24 rather than block domains for a French court
events.summary: The Swiss nonprofit DNS resolver says a French court, in a case brought by broadcaster beIN, ordered it to block certain domain names for users in France, with the daily penalty reduced from €580,000 to €1,000. Quad9 says it cannot comply…

events.headline: NVIDIA's OpenShell, an Apache-2.0 runtime, sandboxes autonomous agents under declared policies
events.summary: OpenShell runs each agent in a kernel-isolated sandbox, checks every network connection against policy, and injects credentials only on requests to approved endpoints so agents never see them. The repository lists SDKs for Python, TypeScri…

events.headline: Anthropic says Claude produced machine-checked memory-safety proofs for 239 entry points across 123 open-source libraries
events.summary: Anthropic reports Claude proved, at the RISC-V assembly level, that the programs never crash from memory-safety errors or failed assertions for any input under 64 MB, using about 180 million lines of Rocq proof and finding hundreds of bugs…

events.summary: Pete Cooper posted that he published details of PHP remote-code-execution bugs CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 before the coordinated disclosure date, writing that he knew of no embargo. Commenters in the thread say the post pushed dis…

events.headline: PHP ships fixes for two remote-code-execution bugs, in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35
events.summary: CVE-2026-109618 corrupts memory when a request hits the memory limit at the wrong moment, and CVE-2026-109619 leaves stale state pointing at freed memory after a fatal error. The PHP Foundation says unauthenticated requests could trigger t…

events.headline: DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS adds a client-server protocol, async I/O and an agent-friendly CLI
events.summary: The release adds the Quack protocol and a CONNECT statement, background reads for Parquet and CSV, a columnar VARIANT type and a PEG-based parser. The CLI detects coding agents and switches to compact Markdown output with JSON errors.

events.headline: Anthropic opens a waitlist for Claude Duet, a proactive background agent powered by Opus 5.5
events.summary: Duet, in research preview, works on tasks in the background, sends morning briefs and asks before sensitive actions such as sending messages or paying. It connects to more than 6,000 connectors and runs on iOS, Android and the web.

events.headline: A compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI installed a credential stealer and backdoor

events.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme says private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were tiny values such as 4, 56 or 115, so at most 255 guesses recover one. Chrome and Firefox blocked the intermediates within hours of the Oct.…

events.headline: UNEP: the Paris 1.5°C goal is no longer achievable; it now frames the aim as overshoot then return
events.summary: The 2026 Emissions Gap Report says exceeding 1.5°C is imminent and calls for cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 versus 2025. Current pledges would deliver only 5–8% by 2030, and about 320 gigatons of CO2 would need removing b…

events.headline: Ofcom concedes it cannot collect every Online Safety Act fine abroad, per 4chan's lawyer
events.summary: Ofcom chief Melanie Dawes told MPs 'we won't be able to recover every single fine on online safety'. Preston Byrne, counsel to 4chan, says a US court ruled against 4chan on sovereign immunity but suggested it would likely not enforce a UK…

events.headline: Mistral ships Voxtral 3: transcription, realtime and text-to-speech models plus a voice-agent SDK
events.summary: The family covers Small and Mini batch transcription (50+ languages), a realtime model with under 500 ms latency, and Mini TTS in 35+ languages. Batch transcription is priced from $0.0035 per minute, and Mistral's own FLEURS benchmark puts…

events.summary: The Apache-2.0 repo offers custom ATen kernels, torch.compile integration, a compilation cache and data and tensor parallelism, with example Llama, Qwen and UNet models. It requires Python 3.11+, and its dependencies section is still marke…

events.headline: Feds suspect a ransom negotiator ran ShinyHunters' Shinywire extortion site
events.summary: Krebs reports Canadian security executive Edward Dubrovsky has been charged with extortion-related offences, and prosecutors want him held pending trial. Shinywire listed nearly 100 victims between May and October; the FBI says the group h…

events.headline: WhatsApp's help pages hid instructions for its support chatbot, including not to point users to regulators
events.summary: Data-deletion firm Redact found hidden AI text on 80 of 545 help pages it read; one reportedly told the bot not to recommend contacting a data protection authority. WhatsApp told WIRED it was a bug, since fixed, and that the bot should avo…

events.summary: The backdoor took about $8 of compute, sits in roughly 0.6% of parameters, and fetches its payload from a URL that can be changed later. The authors suggest runtime sandboxing and vetting weight diffs rather than trusting benchmarks or sca…

events.headline: MiniMax releases M3.1 Flash, priced at $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens
events.summary: MiniMax says the agent-focused model is nearly three times faster than its predecessor, at 200+ tokens per second, and scores 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 82% on CyberGym. It is available through the API now; weights are promised later.

events.headline: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference engine it says runs its production services
events.summary: The Apache-2.0 repo supports DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs, with speculative decoding, expert parallelism and structured outputs. It is offline inference only: no KV cache system, prefill/decode disagg…

events.headline: RepRapMicron: a desktop 3D-printed machine for micron-scale fabrication
events.summary: The open-source μRepRap's PIKA V0.02 achieves about 1 μm repeatable positioning and roughly 10 μm accuracy in an 8 mm cube, depositing UV resin droplets down to 4 μm.

events.headline: Mistral releases Timestral, time-series models that forecast on a CPU
events.summary: Timestral is a family of four models (5M to 209M parameters) producing probabilistic forecasts with a 32,768-step context. Mistral says the 209M model ranks first among pre-trained zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench.

events.headline: Linux 7.3 ships with a record 18,765 commits
events.summary: Torvalds called the release a record-breaker: 18,765 non-merge commits from 3,021 developers, 807 of them first-timers. Additions include fchroot(), global per-CPU data for BPF and a completed sched_ext subscheduler.

events.headline: Karri Saarinen: software needs 'someone behind' it
events.summary: The post argues good products carry the experience and judgment of their makers, a 'soul', and that recent products feel messy because features pile up, often built independently by AI agents.

events.headline: Hybrid Reasoning Agents switch between latent reasoning and text tool use
events.summary: HybridAgents move between latent reasoning and text-based tool calls in one generation. Across 11 benchmarks the authors report 10.4% better performance, 35.5–54.7% fewer tokens and 1.8–2.6× faster inference.

events.headline: A programming language built to defeat LLMs, and the models that struggled
events.summary: KillSwitch hides lies in its spec, enforces letter-count rules and plants guardrail-triggering text. The best benchmark score was 66.8 by Claude Opus 5; some models did poorly because of oversensitive safety guardrails.

events.headline: Llmspeed estimates how fast a local LLM will feel on a given device before you buy
events.summary: The open-source site lets users browse by hardware or model and estimates speed for a short prompt on a single device. Measured figures come from community benchmarks; the rest are derived from similar setups or projected from specs.

events.headline: Lean 4.35 ships verified-kernel tooling, including a Claude-built kernel proven consistent
events.summary: Lean v4.35.0 adds `lake check` to re-verify projects with the official kernel in a sandbox, and `--paranoid` to recheck with four more kernels. One, con-leche, is a Lean kernel proven consistent against a set-theory model, implemented by C…

events.headline: DeepSeek puts Search and Fetch APIs on the meter at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests
events.summary: DeepSeek's docs describe a Search API and a Fetch API, each billed at $0.75 per 1,000 requests that return usable results; failures and timeouts are free. Calls via DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code or Codex are free until billing starts on 1…

events.headline: A blog post argues transformers are best read as associative memory, with attention storing about 1.2 million memories
events.summary: Alex Wang's post frames linear layers, MLPs and self-attention as associative-memory stores whose capacity is set by interference. It puts plain outer-product storage near d_k memories, squared-ReLU MLPs near 2,700 at d_k=64, and softmax a…

events.headline: A New York lawmaker announces a bill to require game ownership rather than licensing
events.summary: Tom's Hardware reports that a New York representative announced a bill that would require games to be sold as owned products rather than licenses, and require publishers to keep games functional after support ends. The retrievable text gav…

events.headline: Mercor estimates about 90% of US working hours go to tasks AI benchmarks barely cover
events.summary: Mercor mapped 29 benchmarks onto 923 O*NET occupations and 18,797 tasks. It estimates about 90% of US working hours fall on tasks with little or no benchmark coverage, and six job families have no well-covered occupation.

events.headline: DeepSeek ships V4.1 Flash 1017, an MIT-licensed 763B-parameter update with a 1M-token context
events.summary: The new checkpoint is billed as a minor update aimed at reasoning, coding and agentic tasks, with shorter outputs. By DeepSeek's own numbers, Terminal-Bench 4.0 rises from 31.2 to 42.3 and HLE without tools from 36.8 to 42.6.

events.headline: Claude Code team: stop reading every line, minimise human review time without raising reverts
events.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code team says Claude writes about 90% of its code, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September while the revert share fell by more than 40%. Review is layered: automated agents, security review, CI, then risk-ti…

events.headline: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6B image model that runs in 8GB of VRAM
events.summary: The model handles text-to-image, editing and up to 10 reference images, with native 4K and bounding-box control. BFL says the distilled INT8 build makes a 1MP image in about 4 seconds on an RTX 5090.
